requirements.statement: Work from an old epoch never mutates the state of the current epoch.
Logical time never moves backwards during normal operation.
A terminal event never returns to a non-terminal state.
requirements.note: terminal_event_rejects_every_transition builds a real event, so it allocates: on macOS with Kani 0.67 it hits the known 'malloc with missing definition' limitation recorded in the README and only verifies where the allocator is modelled.

requirements.statement: await-idle must not return while causal work (including child enqueue reservations and Text Index backfill) is active.
After a reset begins, the new epoch eventually becomes Active.
Under finite retries and fair workers, every event reaches success, dead-letter or cancellation.
When external input stops and work is finite, await-idle eventually returns.
A request that violates a limit or a unique index changes no document, index, outbox or quota state.
requirements.note: Disposition engine and boundary semantics are implemented; the atomic rejection on the commit path arrives with the Firestore core (Milestone E), and LimitRejection.tla is pending with it.

requirements.statement: The write set of one commit is applied entirely or not at all.
When a trigger-relevant change is published, the corresponding logical event exists in the outbox.
Transaction writes are never partially visible.
A generation number is never reused for the same object.
A query accepted as UseIndex by the conservative validator has a supporting index.
requirements.note: Conservative validator implemented in fireemu-core-firestore; the Kani harness and reference-rule conformance fixtures are pending.

requirements.statement: A request that exceeds the expression, document access or call depth budget never reaches allow.
Rules budgets are isolated per request and operation.
A ruleset becomes active only after parse, compile and limit checks; each request observes one immutable version.
A READY Text Index represents every document version its visibility policy and watermark require.
Search never observes a mix of old posting with new document or new posting with old document.
Search never selects a CREATING or NEEDS_REPAIR text index.
Old-epoch backfill or repair workers never change new-epoch index state, postings or watermark.
Unsupported Pipeline stages, including update(...)/delete() output stages, are rejected explicitly and never skipped.
Pipeline Rules never treat a SearchExpr as a narrowing authorization constraint.
Required terms are ANDed and excluded terms remove matches.
Enterprise Core Queries without an index become full-scan plans and unique index violations are rejected atomically.
Due schedules are enqueued unless the skip policy applies.
Static Rules limits (arguments 7, recursion 0, source size < 256 KiB) are enforced at the documented boundaries.
requirements.note: Static linter implemented in fireemu-core-rules; projects.test conformance pending.

requirements.statement: Object names are never normalized and percent-decoded exactly once.
A TOTP code for a time step at or below the last accepted step is never accepted again.
requirements.note: The Kani harness is pending: the acceptance window is decided from HMAC-SHA1 codes and from a 128-bit division in time_step, which bounded model checking does not finish in usable time. The window and replay boundary are covered by AuthTotp.tla, prop_same_step_same_code and the RFC 6238 vectors in crates/fireemu-core-auth/tests/totp.rs.

requirements.statement: An ID token carries sign_in_second_factor only when the user has an enrolled factor that was verified.
TOTP shared secrets never appear in Debug output, canonical traces or default snapshots.
A started TOTP enrollment eventually finalizes or expires under finite clock advance.

App Check defaults preserve current behaviour, and invalid keys, types, service modes, token TTLs, app IDs, project numbers and debug-token digests fail closed in both the canonical JSON Schema and the Rust loader.
requirements.note: The loader delegates every binding rule to the core registry, so the schema, the loader and the runtime cannot disagree; tools/config-schema-check checks the same rules over spec/config/examples and spec/config/invalid-examples.

requirements.statement: Valid, malformed, forged, expired, future-issued, wrong-key, wrong-project, unknown-app, disabled-app and wrong-epoch App Check tokens classify correctly under the virtual clock.
requirements.note: prop_app_check_foreign_keys_never_verify covers INV-APPCHECK-011 alongside the window property; the real RSA key isolation is checked in crates/fireemu-adapter-http/tests/app_check.rs.

requirements.statement: Only a constant-time digest match produces an App Check token, and an invalid app, project and debug secret are externally indistinguishable.
requirements.note: The exchange scans the fixed-capacity digest set without an early exit and performs equivalent dummy work for an unknown app; that limits timing differences and does not claim resistance to a local process-level side channel.

requirements.statement: Duplicate, comma-folded, empty, oversized and otherwise ambiguous X-Firebase-AppCheck values are refused consistently, and no adapter selects one of several values.
requirements.note: Milestone AC0 implemented and proved the transport-neutral classifier; AC1 adopted it on the Firebase Auth HTTP surface, the Storage HTTP surface, Firestore unary gRPC metadata and Firestore REST; AC2 adopted it on the WebChannel init header block -- where the parser now keeps every instance in wire order instead of collapsing them into a map -- and on the callable Functions proxy, where an ambiguous field list is never a credential and is stripped before the runner can decode it. Every transport covers duplicate, folded, empty and oversized values.

requirements.statement: An App Check denial happens before Security Rules and before every side effect: no user, credential, OOB or phone code, MFA change, object generation, upload session, Firestore mutation, event or rules document-access budget consumption survives it.
requirements.note: Each product is checked independently: Auth by an observable absence (no user, a refresh token that still works, an MFA assertion that still finalizes), Storage by an unchanged object store and an unconsumed upload-session identifier, Firestore by the App Check reason preceding a rules denial the same request would also have earned.

requirements.statement: End-user Identity Toolkit and Secure Token routes enforce the configured App Check baseline; Admin and emulator inspection routes follow the explicit bypass; a denial consumes no credential and no action code.
requirements.note: The published route classification is `identity_toolkit::end_user_operation`, which also bounds the observation label. Both bypasses require their own credential: the Admin routes the owner credential, the emulator inspection routes the control token. The latter is checked by the App Check path itself because the routes' own guard only challenges browser requests, so an Origin-less caller would otherwise bypass unguarded.

requirements.statement: Firestore unary gRPC, Write, Listen, REST and WebChannel obey the same mode and credential matrix and the same stream-lifetime contract.
requirements.note: Milestone AC1 covered unary gRPC and REST; AC2 added the Write and Listen streams and the WebChannel transport with their lifetime contract. A stream classifies its opening metadata once and is decided as soon as its first request names the database, then stays admitted for its whole life: token expiry does not end it, and reconnecting is a new admission. A WebChannel binds to the admitted app and the session epoch of that admission; a later envelope may omit the field, but a replacement for another app or one that does not verify closes the channel. Resolving the Firebase Auth credential no longer fails a stream at open, because the App Check decision is not available yet at that point and section 7.4 puts Auth after it.

requirements.statement: Storage metadata, list, upload, resumable continuation and finalization, download, update, delete, the JSON API bypass and the download-token bypass are explicit.
requirements.note: Milestone AC1 covered the non-resumable operations and admitted every resumable request; AC2 bound the session to the app that started it. An enforced initiation records the admitted app and the epoch of that admission in the upload session, and every later request on it -- continuation, status query, cancel and finalization -- must present a valid token for the same app; the check runs before the command is read, so a refused request neither advances nor deletes the upload and token expiry mid-upload preserves the resumable state. Only an enforced policy binds: under unenforced a client may legitimately stop presenting a token, and binding it would enforce by the back door. The download token is compared in constant time and must bind to the resolved bucket, object name and generation. The JSON API bypass requires the owner credential: the dialect bypasses Security Rules without one, as the official Emulator does, but a path shape is not a credential and would otherwise let a caller defeat enforcement by rewriting /v0/b/... to /storage/v1/b/...

requirements.statement: Callable Functions expose valid app context, refuse a missing or invalid token when enforceAppCheck is set, invoke the handler with app undefined when it is not, never let an unverified Auth credential become callable auth context, forward the raw App Check field to onRequest functions, and fail closed on an unsupported consumeAppCheckToken.
requirements.note: The daemon proxy is the trust boundary: the SDK wrapper decodes both callable credentials without verifying either under the skipTokenVerification debug feature, so the daemon verifies first and strips every caller-supplied copy of the fields it owns -- the App Check field, Authorization, the runner secret and the x-callable-context-auth / x-original-auth channels firebase-functions honours to override v1 callable auth context. The integration test asserts on the bytes that actually reach the runner, through an echoing runner HTTP server, rather than on the daemon's intent. Three fail-open paths the security review found are closed: the runner refuses every request when it has no per-runner secret instead of serving them unguarded, the runner reports the auth-override header names the installed SDK honours so a renamed one fails startup rather than silently escaping the proxy's strip list, and a configured functions.manifest may not reclassify a callable as an onRequest function and route it around the boundary. consumeAppCheckToken is read by a version-bounded loader instrumentation that hooks onCallHandler, withInit and wrapTraceContext, the one path every v1, v2, builder and genkit spelling passes through; the value is three-valued and never guessed as false.

requirements.statement: The real Firebase Web SDK obtains a local App Check token through CustomProvider and sends it to Firestore, Storage, Auth and a callable function.
requirements.note: tools/sdk-smoke/appcheck.mjs runs in plain Node without browser shims: CustomProvider touches no browser global and the SDK guards its indexedDB token cache. The SDK never dials the local exchange itself, because @firebase/app-check hard-codes the production base URL, so the documented provider calls the daemon and returns the JWT with an expiry derived from the ttl. It is a manual smoke rather than a CI gate: it needs node_modules and a running daemon, like every other script in tools/sdk-smoke.

requirements.statement: Reset, restore, project deletion and session isolation invalidate or isolate App Check tokens and counters as specified.
requirements.note: Creating, resetting and deleting a project rotates its epoch through the ProjectHooks seam; a snapshot restore replaces the scope's dynamic debug-token registrations and then rotates the epoch. The epochs are drawn from the operating system CSPRNG in the probe phase, before the first store is wiped and before any registration is replaced, so a failing draw leaves the session exactly as it was rather than a wiped session still admitting its old tokens; the installation is one write under the exclusive admission barrier.

requirements.statement: App Check metrics distinguish valid, missing, invalid, bypass, admitted and denied without exposing a secret, and never create a metric label from unverified input.
requirements.note: The registry keeps one bounded ring and one set of counters per project, created on first use and dropped whole when the project's state is cleared (reset, project deletion, snapshot restore), so a flood of requests to one project never evicts another project's recent observations and the counters reset with the state they describe. Counters are keyed by service, verified app ID (or the bounded unknown label), callable function name for the functions service, category and outcome, and they count every classified request since the last reset rather than only what the ring still holds. GET /v1/sessions/{session}/appCheck/observations serves the session's project alone, requires the control token for every method whatever the Origin and sets Cache-Control: no-store; the Emulator UI page at /ui/appcheck and the same-origin fronts behind it (GET /ui/api/appcheck/config, the debug-token routes, and the observation route through the control front) are each Cache-Control: no-store, and a generated debug secret reaches the page in the creation response alone. The table of rings is bounded in turn (at most 256 projects, no ring for an ID no session could name, a registered project displacing the least recently used unregistered one), because a target project is resolved from a request path before anything validates it. Core ring isolation: heavy_traffic_to_one_project_never_evicts_another_projects_observations, counters_outlive_the_observations_the_ring_evicted, clearing_observations_touches_only_the_named_scope, deleting_a_project_drops_its_ring_and_a_later_request_opens_a_fresh_one, callable_counters_group_by_function_and_other_services_do_not, an_unregistered_project_never_displaces_a_registered_ones_ring, an_unnameable_project_id_opens_no_ring. Control route scoping: a_session_reads_only_its_own_projects_observations, one_projects_flood_never_shortens_another_projects_window, counters_group_callables_by_function_name, unknown_token_input_does_not_create_an_unbounded_metrics_label. UI front: the_observation_front_serves_only_the_selected_sessions_project.

requirements.statement: The capability manifest states every APPCHECK-* capability with its status and precision, the surfaces and bypasses App Check enforcement covers, the published local divergences, and that replay protection and production attestation providers are unsupported.
requirements.note: crates/fireemu/tests/capabilities.rs reads GET /v1/capabilities from a daemon started on ephemeral ports, so the assertions cover what the shipped binary publishes rather than the constant behind it. It pins the status and precision of all nine capabilities of specification section 6, refuses an undeclared APPCHECK-* entry, and checks that the enforcement entry names the three baseline modes, the supported product surfaces and transports and every row of the bypass matrix of section 12.2 with the credential it requires; that the fireemu_epoch and JWKS no-store divergences are published; and that the unsupported entries say how they fail closed.

requirements.statement: Selected official-emulator fixtures record App Check header handling, failures, bypasses and callable context, and every row that needs production behaviour is recorded as pending rather than invented.
requirements.note: conformance/ runs one corpus against the official Local Emulator Suite (firebase-tools pinned to an exact version, provenance regenerated into conformance/ORACLE.md) and against fireemu, then records each step as parity, documented-divergence, debt or pending. The App Check rows cover the exchange and JWKS routes and the X-Firebase-AppCheck matrix (missing / valid / unverifiable / duplicate) across Firestore REST, the Identity Toolkit end-user route, the Storage Firebase dialect, an enforcing callable, a non-enforcing callable and an onRequest function, both with enforcement off and with fireemu enforcing. It is partial, not implemented, because the obligation names production fixtures too: the official emulators implement no App Check surface, so what a real project denies under enforcement, the claims on a production limited-use token, and the exact set of Identity Toolkit methods App Check protects are recorded as pending with the reason "needs a real project". No precision is raised on this evidence; conformance/DEBT.md carries the standing proposal for a credentialed second oracle.

requirements.statement: The official oracle is pinned by exact version with recorded provenance, and a fixture can never claim an oracle the tree did not produce.
requirements.note: conformance/package.json pins firebase-tools, firebase, firebase-admin and firebase-functions to exact versions and pnpm-lock.yaml pins their integrity. conformance/ORACLE.md is regenerated by the recorder from the installed CLI: the resolved firebase-tools version, the lockfile integrity string, a digest of the installed manifest, and every bundled downloadable emulator with its upstream SHA-256, read from the CLI's own downloadableEmulatorInfo.json. Partial: the pin covers the Node toolchain this slice exercises. Test images, non-Node SDK artifacts and the Linux / Windows matrix rows of the issue are not pinned yet, and upgrading the pin still requires re-recording by hand rather than an automated delta gate.

requirements.statement: The differential comparison normalizes only documented nondeterminism and compares statuses, error codes and messages, payload shapes, listener sequences and Rules decisions, with a process-level failing exit on drift.
requirements.note: conformance/src/normalize.mjs erases exactly five classes of value -- RFC 3339 instants, twenty-character generated ids, JWTs, UUID-shaped opaque codes and object generations -- plus the host:port the two sides deliberately bind differently; ordering is normalized only where a scenario opts in and the ordering is documented as unspecified. Everything else is compared. `pnpm -C conformance run check` exits non-zero on a parity row that drifted, a documented divergence that moved off its recorded fireemu value, a step no fixture describes, a step that vanished, a pending row that produced an observation, or a scenario that faulted; debt rows are reported and never gate. conformance/src/diff.test.mjs proves each of those without an emulator. Partial: events, logs, exported files, environment variables and process exit behaviour are compared only where a scenario already covers them, and the corpus is Node-only.

requirements.statement: Every word of the public compatibility claim has a testable definition: the claim sentence, the pinned baseline it is qualified by, the products it enumerates and the profile it holds under are one machine-readable contract, and the README may not state it differently.
requirements.note: spec/compatibility/contract.json carries the claim sentence, the pinned firebase-tools 15.28.2 baseline with its lockfile integrity, installed manifest digest, bundled emulator versions and the 2026-08-30 audit date, the official documentation URLs, and the two compatibility profiles. tools/compat-check CC-05 fails when README.md does not carry that sentence verbatim (whitespace-normalized, so wrapping is allowed) and CC-08 fails when a profile names a key or a value spec/config/fireemu.schema.json does not define, or when the profile names the contract declares are not exactly the values that schema's profile key accepts. The profile is now a runtime switch rather than a declared key set: the schema's top-level profile key takes firebase (the default, the profile the claim is made under) or strict, the loader derives firestore.indexValidationPolicy, firestore.enforceLimits and the ID-token semantics of the Security Rules surfaces from it with any explicit key winning, fireemu capabilities and GET /v1/capabilities publish the active profile and the banner prints it. the_same_official_limitation_is_served_under_firebase_and_refused_under_strict runs one official limitation under both profiles against a started daemon. The keys each profile declares but the loader does not yet derive are listed in the contract's profileStatus. An upstream upgrade is fail-closed in three places: CC-02 compares baseline.version with the version conformance/package.json installs, requires the claim sentence to name it, and keeps failing until any surface the new release adds is enumerated with a scope.

requirements.statement: Every official product and orchestration emulator of the pinned firebase-tools release is inventoried in the contract with a scope, a state and a recorded decision, and a surface can neither be forgotten nor invented.
requirements.note: The contract's baseline.officialEmulators is the fifteen-name inventory of firebase-tools 15.28.2 src/emulator/types.ts (hub, ui, logging, extensions, apphosting, auth, functions, firestore, database, hosting, pubsub, storage, eventarc, dataconnect, tasks), together with the service, downloadable and import/export subsets. tools/compat-check CC-02 fails when an inventory name is enumerated by no surface, when two surfaces claim the same one, and when a surface names an emulator the baseline does not ship; CC-01 fails on a duplicate surface or claim id, an unknown scope or state and a surface with no recorded decision. Two fireemu additions (App Check, the control API) are enumerated as surfaces with official: false so they can never be counted as official parity.

requirements.statement: Extra strictness cannot masquerade as parity: every behaviour in which fireemu refuses what the official emulator admits is published with its own precision, and the compatibility profile that reproduces official behaviour is separated from the one that adds validation.
requirements.note: Each claim in the contract separates the documented official limitations it must reproduce, the fireemu-only behaviours with their precision, the production-only behaviour that is out of scope, and the preview surfaces whose compatibility is narrower. conformance/divergences.json remains the executed half: a row may only leave debt by naming the text that publishes it, and check gates it against the recorded fireemu value. The both-profile scenario now exists as a test: the_same_official_limitation_is_served_under_firebase_and_refused_under_strict starts a daemon under each profile and asserts that the unindexed query the pinned official Firestore emulator serves is served under firebase and refused under strict with the firestore.indexes.json fragment, so only strict adds the rejection. The same shape is proved for the other two derived settings: the_limit_switch_turns_a_refusal_into_an_observation for Standard query limits, and the mock-token tests on all three Rules surfaces (the_firebase_profile_admits_the_mock_tokens_the_official_emulator_admits on gRPC, the_profile_decides_whether_rest_admits_a_mock_token on REST, the_profile_decides_whether_storage_rules_admit_a_mock_token on Storage) with the_strict_profile_refuses_a_mock_token_the_auth_store_cannot_verify as the strict half. Where the firebase profile cannot match the official emulator exactly -- it still binds a token's audience to the project and still verifies a signed token -- the contract records both as officialEmulatorDivergences of that profile rather than leaving the strictness implicit.

requirements.statement: An upstream capability the manifest calls implemented and that no executed test or conformance fixture exercises fails the claim gate, and so does a stale evidence name.
requirements.note: tools/compat-check CC-03 requires every manifest capability whose status is implemented or partial to be bound by a claim to at least one evidence item that resolves, and reports every item that does not resolve in its own right so a stale name cannot hide behind a live one. Evidence resolves the way tools/traceability-check resolves it: a tests name is a function defined under a tests/ directory, an integration name is a repository-relative file that exists, and a conformance name is a fixture under conformance/fixtures/. All thirty-five manifest entries are bound. The fixture table proves each failure shape: no evidence at all, a ghost test function, a deleted integration file and a fixture id with no fixture.

requirements.statement: The README, the capability manifest and the executed evidence cannot contradict each other: an item one public statement calls unimplemented may not be called implemented by another.
requirements.note: tools/compat-check CC-04 fails when a claim and the manifest disagree on a capability's status, when a claim names a capability the manifest does not declare, and when a manifest entry appears in no claim. CC-07 catches the contradiction class this issue named, in two shapes: an unimplemented item that cross-references another capability the manifest declares implemented (ST-OBJ-1 listed "Storage triggers (FN-EVT-1)" while FN-EVT-1 listed them implemented), and a term of the contract's shared vocabulary written with the wrong status anywhere -- in an implemented list, in an unimplemented list, or denied in the README (the README said ExecutePipeline was not implemented while FS-PIPE-RPC-1 declared validation-only support implemented). Both contradictions are fixed: the cross-references moved into notes and the README now states the validation-only semantics.

requirements.statement: The active / deferred / not-planned scope taxonomy is enforced: a deferred or not-planned product may never read as supported in the manifest or in the README, and no complete-suite or unqualified superset wording may stand while one is in the pinned baseline.
requirements.note: Realtime Database, Firebase Hosting and App Hosting are deferred and Firebase Extensions is not planned; each declares the terms that may not read as supported. tools/compat-check CC-06 fails when such a term appears in any manifest entry's implemented list, when a README line names it without a scope disclaimer on the same line, when a non-active surface carries a parity claim at all, and when a non-active surface declares no prohibited terms, which would leave it unpoliced. The claim sentence of the contract is itself product-enumerated and version-qualified and says plainly that no complete-suite and no unqualified superset claim is made while those four surfaces are in the baseline; CC-05 keeps the README from stating anything else.

requirements.statement: A firebase.json fireemu accepts is one the daemon can load, and one it refuses is refused with the path that is wrong and no partial startup.
requirements.note: spec/config/firebase-json.schema.json and the two corpora under spec/config/firebase-json-examples and spec/config/firebase-json-invalid-examples are validated by tools/config-schema-check and replayed through RuntimeConfig::apply_firebase_json by the_firebase_json_corpus_agrees_with_the_loader, so the schema and the loader cannot drift. crates/fireemu/tests/cli.rs drives the shipped binary over a real project directory: a_project_alias_from_firebaserc_resolves_the_project, config_accepts_a_firebase_json_as_well_as_the_canonical_configuration, a_multi_codebase_functions_section_names_the_codebase_to_load, a_named_firestore_database_is_reported_rather_than_folded_into_the_default_one, a_routable_emulator_host_is_refused and a_command_line_port_overrides_the_one_in_firebase_json. Partial: a named Firestore database's own rules and indexes, a per-target Storage ruleset and a second Functions codebase are reported rather than loaded.

requirements.statement: A service --only did not name binds no listener and exports no variable, and a service it did name exports exactly the canonical variables of the official CLI.
requirements.note: an_unselected_service_binds_no_listener_at_all probes each configured port from inside the running command, so silence is asserted while the daemon is serving rather than inferred. every_selection_exports_exactly_the_canonical_variables_of_its_services pins the names and the formats against firebase-tools@15.28.2 src/emulator/env.ts, including that STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST carries a scheme and FIREBASE_STORAGE_EMULATOR_HOST does not, and that FIREBASE_DATABASE_EMULATOR_HOST is never set. an_occupied_port_of_a_selected_service_fails_before_the_command_runs is the negative case: a busy port of a selected service refuses the run, and the same port is usable when that service was left out. the_control_plane_leaves_the_auth_port_free_when_auth_is_not_selected covers the one shared socket, and inherited_emulator_variables_do_not_reach_the_command_unless_selected covers the clearing.

requirements.statement: An official Local Emulator Suite service fireemu does not serve is never silently ignored: selecting it fails with its scope status before anything binds.
requirements.note: an_official_service_fireemu_does_not_serve_is_refused_with_its_status (crates/fireemu/tests/exec.rs) covers all eight products and checks that the command never ran, and that hub, ui and logging are refused as non-service names. a_deferred_emulator_entry_is_a_notice_unless_only_asks_for_it (crates/fireemu/tests/cli.rs) covers the other half of the rule, that an emulators.<name> entry alone is a notice rather than a failure. the_only_list_names_services_and_at_most_one_functions_codebase drives the same table through the parser, iterating the UNSERVED_OFFICIAL_SERVICES constant itself so a product added there without a status fails the test.

requirements.statement: Official tooling discovers the running suite through the Emulator Hub without being told a single host or port.
requirements.note: the_hub_publishes_every_running_emulator_in_the_official_shape drives GET /emulators, GET /, the 404 and 501 routes and the loopback-Host guard over a real socket, and asserts that nothing which is not running is advertised. the_locator_file_is_written_at_start_and_removed_at_exit covers the locator's life, exec_exports_the_hub_address_to_its_command the exported variable's format, and a_daemon_that_could_not_bind_the_hub_serves_the_suite_anyway the best-effort port rule. tools/sdk-smoke/rules-unit-testing.mjs is the end-to-end proof: @firebase/rules-unit-testing 5.0.2 with an empty configuration reaches Firestore through the Hub alone, and exercises withSecurityRulesDisabled and clearFirestore there.

requirements.statement: While background triggers are disabled no data-change event is delivered, and re-enabling them delivers nothing retroactively.
requirements.note: the drop-rather-than-hold semantics match firebase-tools@15.28.2 functionsEmulator.ts, whose background-trigger route answers 204 and discards the body while the producing emulators keep posting. the_hub_switches_background_triggers_and_says_so covers the routes and their bodies with and without a functions codebase; tools/sdk-smoke/rules-unit-testing.mjs covers the behaviour, writing a document while triggers are off, waiting for the runtime to go idle, and asserting the trigger neither ran then nor after the switch came back, with a later write proving the triggers really returned.

requirements.statement: The command surface reports what happened: the exec command's status is propagated, a signal becomes 128 + signal, a refused configuration or an unsupported feature exits 1 without starting anything, and a usage error exits 2.
requirements.note: the_official_command_names_are_aliases_of_the_short_ones, export_is_refused_precisely_rather_than_reported_as_unknown, import_and_export_on_exit_fail_before_anything_starts, log_verbosity_decides_whether_the_banner_is_printed and inspect_functions_passes_the_node_inspector_through_to_the_runner (crates/fireemu/tests/cli.rs) pin the codes and check that a refusal leaves no marker behind. The signal half is covered by sigterm_stops_the_command_and_the_services_without_leaving_processes and sigint_keeps_its_identity_when_forwarded (crates/fireemu/tests/exec.rs), which also assert that nothing is left listening or running.

requirements.statement: Every builtin, namespace, operator, coercion, comparison and regex construct of the Firestore Rules language answers what the pinned official runtime answers, or diverges only where the divergence is recorded.
requirements.note: Measured, not asserted: conformance/src/rules-probe installs bounded Rules programs into the official Firestore emulator and into fireemu through the same route and compares the verdict of each. 680 claims, 260 of them generated from a seed and shrunk on mismatch; three rows are documented divergences where the official compiler rejects statically what fireemu raises at evaluation.

requirements.statement: The request and resource models a rule sees -- request.auth, request.method, request.path, request.time, request.resource, request.query and resource -- are present, absent or null exactly as the official runtime makes them.
requirements.note: Firestore is measured by the same differential probe: request.resource and request.query are absent rather than null when the request has none, request.query.orderBy is a map from field path to ASC / DESC, and request.keys() lists exactly what the official runtime lists. The Storage request model is not probed differentially yet.

requirements.statement: Query authorization, atomic-write authorization, document-access budgets and the call-graph limits reach the same decision as the official runtime, and the call-graph limits are reported when the ruleset loads rather than when a request arrives.
requirements.note: Ten distinct document accesses are served and eleven are denied; a path read repeatedly is charged once; a recursive call and a call chain of more than twenty calls are compile errors with the official messages; a list rule that reads a field the query does not constrain is denied and one the query does constrain is served. All twenty-two program probes agree with the pinned emulator on status, code and payload shape.

requirements.statement: Rules evaluation is observable: the official :ruleCoverage and :ruleCoverage.html endpoints report every expression by its source position with the values it took, and a privileged control route lists the last decided requests with their per-expression traces and no secret.
requirements.note: The report is keyed by (line, column, currentOffset, endOffset) as the official one is; an expression that raised contributes an undefined value naming the innermost expression that raised; an expression nothing reached has children and no values. The diagnostics live inside the loaded ruleset, so replacing it replaces them.

requirements.statement: @firebase/rules-unit-testing runs unmodified against fireemu: Hub discovery, authenticated and unauthenticated contexts, withSecurityRulesDisabled, clear operations, trigger suppression and loading rules through the emulator's own securityRules route.
requirements.note: The library's documented flows run with no explicit host anywhere (tools/sdk-smoke/rules-unit-testing.mjs). Its coverage-report helpers are served by the :ruleCoverage endpoints; the library's own assertion helpers over that report are not exercised yet.
